## EA Media Tools 1.0.0 — ea-video

### Select exactly what gets processed

- Video, Audio, and Subtitles now have independent processing switches, enabled by default.
- Enabled sections use the selected encode settings; disabled sections copy all source streams in that section without re-encoding.
- This supports combinations such as audio-only processing while video and subtitles pass through unchanged.

### Metadata-only updates

- Unchecking all three processing sections enters metadata-only mode for video, audio, and subtitle streams.
- Edit language plus default, forced, and hearing-impaired dispositions without re-encoding media.
- Batch changes are intentionally per source: only files with an explicit metadata change enter the update queue.
- Smart naming is disabled and the original path is retained. Each update is staged beside its source as `_tmp00`, `_tmp01`, and so on, then safely installed only after FFmpeg succeeds.
- If final replacement fails, EA Media Tools restores the original file; any backup that cannot be cleaned up is retained and recorded in the log.

### Progress and session controls

- Progress titles now include elapsed time.
- **Done** appears only after every job completes, or after an explicit **Cancel all active encodes** request has fully settled.
- **Live FFmpeg Output** follows new commands only when already at the bottom, so scrolling upward is no longer interrupted.

### Updates and release notes

- The startup splash now remains visible with live updater status until the check resolves or an update restart prompt is ready.
- Manual update checks share an already-running automatic check instead of starting a conflicting Squirrel process.
- **View Change Log** in the gear menu opens the installed version's GitHub release notes in a built-in viewer.

### Highlights since v0.3.0

- Added two-file parallel NVENC queues, a 10-second per-slot cooldown, job pagination, individual and queue-wide cancellation, and a redacted session-wide FFmpeg command console.
- Corrected CUVID cropping, strict output scaling profiles, output-tier bitrate/NVENC settings, and automatic buffer-size calculations.
- Upgraded the development and release toolchain to Node.js 24 and current stable compatible dependencies.
- Corrected and coordinated the Windows x64 updater feed and startup/manual checks.

### Validation

- Lint, native TypeScript, TypeScript compatibility checks, and metadata/update/progress/scaling regression tests.
- Windows x64 production package verification before publishing.
- Stable release workflow for Windows, macOS, and Debian on x64 and ARM64.

[Review all changes since v0.3.0](https://github.com/eaforlife/media-converter/compare/v0.3.0...v1.0.0).
